sources: Rep. Thomas Massie (X, Nov 4); President Trump (remarks to reporters, Nov 4); CNN (Nov 4 report, via AJ liveblog / TRT World / Statesman)
fault_line: Scapegoat or architect -- should Hegseth take the fall for a war voters just punished, or is Trump shielding the man who sold him the war?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Massie X, Nov 4] 'There is one contingency in which I won't reintroduce the articles of impeachment: Hegseth resigns.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- CNN via AJ liveblog/TRT World] Massie is expected to introduce the measure when Congress returns next week, with multiple Republican sources indicating the motion is expected to pass; a separate House Republican repudiation vote is expected in days. [PRIMARY-SOURCE QUOTE -- Trump, Nov 4] Asked whether he was considering replacing Hegseth: 'No, I think he's doing a very good job.' White House (Anna Kelly): full confidence; Pentagon (Sean Parnell): Hegseth '100 percent committed' to leading the department until the end of Trump's term (Jan 20, 2029). [ATTRIBUTED -- ANI/Tribune India] Rep. Jason Crow: Hegseth 'needs to go... He's incompetent'; Rep. Patrick Ryan: 'the first job will be getting rid of Hegseth... Right when Congress gets back next week, there will be a privileged resolution vote for impeachment of Pete Hegseth.' [CONTEXT] Massie's original Sept 15 resolution: 34 pages, 8 articles, filed as privileged (vote due within two legislative days); it stalled before a floor vote. [ATTRIBUTED COST FIGURE -- TRT World, origin unstated] 'The war in Iran has cost the US over $47 billion' -- single-outlet figure, NOT independently verified; do not render as a verified number. [BACKGROUND -- CBS, recorded 0000-01] Trump asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay; blame also eyed for CENTCOM chief Cooper and Joint Chiefs chair Caine; DeSantis floated as replacement.
sections.what_verified: Massie ultimatum: AJ liveblog (T2) + TRT World (T3, STATE TR) + Tribune India/ANI relay (T3 via Times of India family) + The Hindu liveblog (T2) + Statesman (undeclared) -- all relay the same X post and CNN report, so corroboration is of the statement's existence/wording, not of the vote outcome. Trump backing: Deccan Herald + The Hindu + Statesman + IndiaTV (all relays of the same Nov 4 remarks; Deccan/Statesman/IndiaTV undeclared tier, do not count).
sections.what_disputed: Trump's public backing contradicts the private deliberation reporting (CBS: Trump asked advisers about replacing Hegseth; one adviser said he 'could be on the chopping block'). A House impeachment vote next week would take place under the outgoing Republican-controlled Congress, so Republican support -- not Democratic -- decides the immediate outcome; the 'expected to pass' claim rests on unnamed Republican sources via CNN. Massie's articles remain allegations, not findings of misconduct.
sections.why_matters: Resign or be impeached: Massie gives Hegseth the ultimatum as Trump says 'very good job' -- the vote lands next week, under the outgoing Republican House.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO 0400-01 / 0200-02 + MISSED CATCH-UP (AJ liveblog 04:30 GMT = 08:30 ; Massie X post Nov 4; CNN Nov 4) -- Massie ultimatum: impeach Hegseth or he resigns; vote expected when Congress returns next week; Trump publicly backs Hegseth ('very good job'); Reps Crow and Ryan join the push
